context.body: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: A blind man asks what the passing crowd means, hears Jesus of Nazareth, cries to the Son of David, persists through rebuke, receives sight, follows, and leads public praise.
observations.label: A blind man calls the Son of David near Jericho: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Jesus, a blind man, the crowd, and those leading, the approach to Jericho and the roadside, inquiring, hearing, crying, rebuking, stopping, asking, seeing, following, and praising visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: A blind man calls the Son of David near Jericho: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Jesus, a blind man, the crowd, and those leading · the approach to Jericho and the roadside · inquiring, hearing, crying, rebuking, stopping, asking, seeing, following, and praising · Davidic address moves from heard identity to restored sight and communal praise
observations.label: Relationships named in Luke 18:35–43

payload.posture: Read Luke 18:35–43 as its own gospel and apostolic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places Davidic address moves from heard identity to restored sight and communal praise inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: A blind man calls the Son of David near Jericho
